_comment: Copy this to `pipeline.config.json` at your PROJECT root and edit. Every value is optional; sensible defaults apply when a key is absent. Grep the plugin for `CUSTOMIZE` to see where each is used.
checkCommand: npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run lint
_migrationGlobs_comment: NOT SET ON PURPOSE. The built-in fifteen-row framework-preset union (Rails, Django, Alembic, Prisma, Drizzle, Supabase, Flyway, Liquibase, EF Core, Laravel, plus the generic declarative dumps) already applies. Setting `migrationGlobs` REPLACES that union for the pre-Phase-4 gate's migration discovery, so a copied one-pattern value would make the gate discover nothing for most layouts while the mis-tier tripwire still fires. To ADD your own layout, set `extraMigrationGlobs` (additive everywhere, never replaces). Set `migrationGlobs` only when you specifically want to NARROW gate discovery.
_dispatchEfforts_comment: NOT SET ON PURPOSE. Per-role reasoning effort (low/medium/high/xhigh/max) for the WORKFLOW dispatch surface only. The Agent tool has no effort parameter, so on today's dispatches agents/<role>.md frontmatter governs and this key changes nothing; it is here for the pending Workflow migration. `secops` and `qa` are pinned in code and ignore this key entirely, at every tier, phase and surface. Example: { "librarian": "high" }.

architecturalTriggers._comment: Domains/keywords that force the architectural tier (deep review). Tailor to your stack.
architecturalTriggers._paths_comment: A diff touching this file is architectural, always. It governs whether the mis-tier tripwire fires, who is seated on the Phase 4 panel, and which model renders a binding verdict. Write access here already implies arbitrary command execution through checkCommand, so this is not a new trust boundary; it is closed because a narrowed glob is quiet and permanent and reads as a tuning change, where an RCE is immediate and loud.
